# C4 Documentation Line

Four documenters that work the C4 levels in order, from reading the source up to the system context diagram.

## How the team works

The routing order is the method. This team works bottom up: the code documenter reads the source and records what is actually there, the component documenter groups those findings into responsibilities, the container documenter maps components onto deployable units, and the context documenter draws the outermost view of the system and its neighbours. Each level takes the level below as input, so no one invents a box that nothing underneath supports. Run it in reverse and you get the architecture somebody wishes existed.

## The roster

- **C4 Code Documenter**: Documents the lowest C4 level by reading source directly: classes, modules, and the relationships the code actually has.
- **C4 Component Documenter**: Rolls code-level findings up into components, naming each responsibility and the interfaces between them.
- **C4 Container Documenter**: Maps components onto deployable containers: the applications, data stores, and the protocols connecting them.
- **C4 Context Documenter** (leads): Draws the outermost C4 view: the system, the people who use it, and every external system it depends on.

## Handoffs

- C4 Code Documenter to C4 Component Documenter, when the code-level pass is complete.
- C4 Component Documenter to C4 Container Documenter, when the components and their interfaces are documented.
- C4 Container Documenter to C4 Context Documenter, when the containers and their connections are documented.
- C4 Context Documenter to C4 Code Documenter, when the context view reveals a dependency nothing in the code explains.
